top_violation_types.title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - installed and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions (26 TAC §746.5625(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The electronic child safety alarm was observed not functioning in one of the operation's vans used to transport the children in care.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation and video, it was found that the caregiver did not demonstrate a high level of judgment or self-control.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The allegation is related to a DFPS abuse/neglect investigation and found to be deficient. Based on interviews with children and daycare staff, it was determined a caregiver used profane language towards children in care.

top_violation_types.title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: No diaper changing tables wwere observed in the infant and toddler's rooms.

top_violation_types.title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two infants did not have current infant feeding schedules.
